Evidence_layer: Unified ECOTOX + WoS quantitative pH metadata
Support: 89 / 304 Results with numeric pH metadata; 61 ECOTOX + 28 WoS
Interpretation: The WoS second pass improves pH metadata coverage substantially, but pH remains incompletely and non-uniformly reported across sources.
Three repeated-pH ECOTOX contexts are present (E_166133, E_107036, E_17219), but salinity changes together with pH in all three; some also contain minor temperature variation.

Support: 7 / 17 References with numeric exposure pH; 28 / 57 retained Results; no verified deliberate pH manipulation; Yang ZnCl2 arm status not separately reported
Interpretation: Numeric test-water pH was source-verifiable for seven quantitative WoS References, but it describes constant/range test conditions rather than a manipulated pH series.
Higher pCO2 was associated with a lower 48-h Cd LC50, but the comparison is retained as CO2-driven acidification evidence; it is not converted into a pH-response slope.
The evidence does not support a general pH coefficient. pH remains a relevant water-chemistry / carbonate-system context variable rather than an independently estimated predictor in this thesis.
